icd11_title: Acute myocardial infarction / Coronary artery disease
name: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) / Myocardial Infarction
etiology_and_causes: Atherosclerosis resulting from fibrofatty plaque buildup inside the coronary arteries, restricting oxygenated myocardial blood flow. Primary risk factors include dyslipidemia (elevated LDL-C), essential hypertension, diabetes mellitus, tobacco smoking, positive family history, physical inactivity, and obesity.

cardinal: Substernal chest pain, pressure, or squeezing sensation ('elephant on chest')
Radiation of discomfort to left shoulder, arm, neck, jaw, or epigastrium
Exertional dyspnea (shortness of breath)
Diaphoresis (cold sweats)
Dizziness, lightheadedness, and profound fatigue
emergency_red_flags: Severe crushing chest pain persisting > 10 minutes
Chest pain accompanied by fainting (syncope) or vomiting
Acute cyanosis or irregular, rapid palpitations with breathlessness

diagnostic_workup: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG) to identify ST-elevation (STEMI) vs non-ST-elevation (NSTEMI)
High-sensitivity cardiac Troponin-I / Troponin-T serial quantitative assays
Transthoracic 2D-Echocardiogram assessing left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and regional wall motion abnormalities
Coronary Catheter Angiography (gold standard for anatomical lesion localization and stenosis grading)

trusted_sources.citation: Arnett DK, et al. 2019 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease. Circulation. 2019;140(11):e596-e646.

name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
etiology_and_causes: Progressive secretory defect of pancreatic beta-cell insulin production on the background of peripheral insulin resistance in skeletal muscle, liver, and adipose tissue. Predisposing factors include central adiposity, genetic predisposition, sedentary lifestyle, gestational diabetes history, and metabolic syndrome.

cardinal: Polyuria (frequent urination, especially nocturnal)
Polydipsia (excessive unquenchable thirst)
Polyphagia (increased hunger with paradoxical weight loss)
Blurred vision and recurring cutaneous or fungal infections
Peripheral neuropathy (tingling, numbness, or burning sensation in feet)
emergency_red_flags: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (blood glucose > 600 mg/dL with confusion)
Diabetic Ketoacidosis (nausea, deep Kussmaul breathing, fruity acetone breath)

diagnostic_workup: Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) >= 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) after 8-hour overnight fast
Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c) >= 6.5% measured in certified laboratory
Two-hour Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) 75g load >= 200 mg/dL
Urinary Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (UACR) for diabetic nephropathy screening
Dilated Fundus Examination for diabetic retinopathy evaluation

related_procedures.waiting_period_type: Pre-Existing Disease (PED) waiting period rules apply

trusted_sources.evidence_summary: Etiology, glycemic control targets, oral hypoglycemic agents, and microvascular prevention.

trusted_sources.citation: ElSayed NA, et al. Standards of Care in Diabetes—2023. Diabetes Care. 2023;46(Suppl 1):S1-S291.

icd11_chapter: 15 - Diseases of the musculoskeletal system or connective tissue
name: Osteoarthritis of Knee Joint
etiology_and_causes: Degeneration of articular hyaline cartilage accompanied by subchondral bone remodeling, osteophyte formation, and mild synovial inflammation. Primary etiology is multifactorial: biomechanical joint overload, advancing age (>50 years), female preponderance, prior cruciate ligament or meniscal tears, and genetic factors.

cardinal: Persistent knee joint pain exacerbated by weight-bearing, stair climbing, or squatting
Joint stiffness in morning or following inactivity, resolving within 30 minutes
Crepitus (grating or crackling noise during joint flexion)
Bony enlargement and progressive varus (bow-legged) deformity
Limitation of range of motion and joint effusion
emergency_red_flags: Sudden acute erythema, warmth, and inability to bear weight (suspect septic arthritis or crystal arthropathy)

diagnostic_workup: Weight-bearing bilateral knee anteroposterior (AP) and lateral plain radiographs
Kellgren-Lawrence grading: Grade 1 (doubtful) to Grade 4 (severe joint space obliteration & large osteophytes)
High-resolution Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) if meniscal tears or osteonecrosis suspected
Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) and Serum Uric Acid to rule out inflammatory/gouty arthropathies

name: Cataract (Senile / Age-Related)
etiology_and_causes: Aggregated and oxidized crystallin protein fibrils inside the crystalline lens, causing progressive opacification and light scattering. Predominantly age-related senescence, accelerated by diabetes mellitus, long-term topical or systemic corticosteroid therapy, ocular trauma, and ultraviolet-B (UVB) radiation exposure.

cardinal: Painless, progressive clouding or blurring of vision ('looking through frosted glass')
Difficulty with night driving due to glare and halos around headlights
Fading or yellowing of color perception
Frequent changes in eyeglass prescriptions
Monocular diplopia (double vision in one eye)
emergency_red_flags: Acute ocular pain with headache, corneal edema, and vomiting (phacomorphic acute angle-closure glaucoma)

diagnostic_workup: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy examining anterior/posterior lens capsule and nucleus density
Visual acuity measurement via Snellen chart with pinhole refraction
Dilated Funduscopy evaluating retina and optic nerve head prior to surgery
Optical or Ultrasound Biometry (A-Scan) calculating Intraocular Lens (IOL) power

trusted_sources.citation: Miller KM, et al. Cataract in the Adult Eye Preferred Practice Pattern. Ophthalmology. 2022;129(1):P1-P126.

name: Chronic Kidney Disease (End-Stage Renal Disease)
etiology_and_causes: Irreversible nephron destruction resulting in glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 15 mL/min/1.73m2. Leading etiologies in India are diabetic nephropathy (30-40%), hypertensive nephrosclerosis, chronic glomerulonephritis, polycystic kidney disease, and analgesic nephropathy.

cardinal: Uremic symptoms: nausea, anorexia, metallic taste, and intractable pruritus (itching)
Oliguria (reduced urine volume) with periorbital and peripheral pedal edema
Refractory hypertension and fluid overload dyspnea
Normocytic normochromic anemia due to erythropoietin deficiency
Cognitive blunting, asterixis, and uremic frost
emergency_red_flags: Severe hyperkalemia (Serum Potassium > 6.5 mEq/L with peaked T waves on ECG)
Uremic pericarditis with pericardial friction rub
Severe pulmonary edema unresponsive to loop diuretics

diagnostic_workup: Serum Creatinine and Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) with eGFR calculation via CKD-EPI formula
Serum Electrolytes (Potassium, Sodium, Bicarbonate, Calcium, Phosphorus)
Urine routine microscopy and 24-hour urinary protein / spot Albumin-to-Creatinine ratio
Renal Ultrasonography demonstrating bilateral small, echogenic shrunken kidneys with loss of corticomedullary differentiation

name: Acute Appendicitis
etiology_and_causes: Luminal obstruction of the vermiform appendix by a fecalith, lymphoid hyperplasia, foreign body, or parasitic infestation, resulting in increased intraluminal pressure, ischemic mucosal necrosis, bacterial invasion, and risk of gangrenous perforation.

cardinal: Vague periumbilical visceral pain migrating and localizing to the Right Lower Quadrant (McBurney's point)
Anorexia (hamburger sign), low-grade pyrexia, and nausea/vomiting
Localized tenderness, guarding, and rebound tenderness in right iliac fossa
Positive Rovsing's, Psoas, and Obturator physical signs
emergency_red_flags: Sudden temporary pain relief followed by diffuse generalized abdominal peritonitis and high fever (indicates perforation)

diagnostic_workup: Complete Blood Count (CBC) showing leukocytosis with neutrophil left-shift (> 10,000 / uL)
High-resolution graded-compression Abdominal Ultrasonography (non-compressible blind-ended tubular structure > 6 mm)
Contrast-enhanced Abdominal & Pelvic Computed Tomography (CECT, sensitivity > 95% in adults)
Serum Beta-hCG in female patients of childbearing age to rule out ruptured ectopic pregnancy
